history.summary: Implemented an operator-triggered, manual, irreversible CLI purge for Event.Details/DetailsCiphertext: --purge-event-details-before <RFC3339> with mutually-exclusive --dry-run/--yes (hard refusal if neither or both given, never a silent default), and --include-active-campaigns (off by default; active campaigns excluded via a single campaign_id IN (SELECT id FROM campaigns WHERE status = 'Completed') subquery). Eligibility is a single shared function (eventDetailsPurgeEligibilityClause) used identically by both the dry-run report and the real purge, so they can never drift. The real purge (models.PurgeEventDetailsBefore) accepts no *credentials.Cipher at all -- decryption is structurally impossible in its call graph, not merely avoided by convention -- and clears both detail columns unconditionally for every row meeting the eligibility rule regardless of LEGACY/MIGRATED/BOTH/INVALID transition state. Reuses PR #68's eventDetailsMigrationBatchSize (500) via one-transaction-per-batch, re-deriving eligibility fresh from row state every batch (no cursor), so it is idempotent, resumable after interruption, and tolerant of concurrent campaign deletion. No new HTTP route, no new dependency, no schema migration, go.mod/go.sum/package.json/yarn.lock byte-identical to base. Pre-implementation re-validation of every goal.md section-0 fact against the current repository found zero discrepancies. Empirically verified (not just statically reasoned) that campaign_results.js's existing `if (event.details)` guard already makes a purged event's empty Details indistinguishable from a never-had-details event: a new real-browser Playwright test (tests/browser/event-details-purge.spec.ts, driven twice by controllers' TestBrowserEventDetailsPurge, with a real direct Go-side purge executed between the two runs against the same live server) proves Replay renders and works pre-purge and is cleanly absent post-purge with zero console/page errors and an intact CSV row -- all with ZERO changes to any frontend file. Test matrix: CLI argument parsing, dry-run zero-writes, all four eligibility rules, all four transition states purged without any decrypt call, multi-batch purging, idempotent re-run, simulated-interruption resume, campaign-stats regression, API-metadata retention, a no-secret-logging proof (synthetic PURGE_TEST_SECRET marker grepped out of every returned value, log buffer, and error string), a real MySQL 8.4 Docker integration test (strict and non-strict SQL modes, same precedent as TestMySQLEventDetailsNearLegacyCapRoundTripsStrictAndNonStrict), and the real-browser regression above. New docs/EVENT_DETAILS_PURGE.md covers the CLI contract, eligibility, mechanics, the logical-deletion-vs-forensic-erasure distinction, backup/keyring caveats, webhook/CSV irrevocability, and the explicit 'no default retention duration exists' statement. Full ./scripts/verify.sh (gofmt, golangci-lint, go vet/build/test/test-race, frontend asset-diff rebuild, action pins, govulncheck) green, plus gosec/gitleaks/actionlint/zizmor all clean with zero new findings versus the established baseline.

Independently verified every binding section of goal.md against the Builder's single commit. Confirmed by direct code read and grep (not Builder claims): eventDetailsPurgeEligibilityClause is the single shared eligibility function used identically by both dry-run and real purge (exactly one repo-wide occurrence of the active-campaign subquery, correctly non-inverted); zero references to internal/credentials, *credentials.Cipher, or any .Decrypt( call anywhere in models/event_details_purge.go, making decryption structurally impossible; main.go's CLI wiring calls ValidateEventDetailsPurgeMode before cutoff parsing, gates on ValidateEventDetailsBackend, and folds the purge action into the existing credentialActions mutual-exclusivity counter. Independently re-ran the full SQLite-backed Go test subset (CLI parsing, dry-run zero-writes, all eligibility rules, all four transition states purged without decrypting, multi-batch, idempotence, interruption/resume, stats regression, API metadata retention, two independent secret-leak marker tests, backend validation) plus go test -race on the same subset -- all PASS, zero races, zero secret leakage. Confirmed zero diff to static/ and to go.mod/go.sum/package.json/yarn.lock via git diff --stat main..HEAD. Read the browser spec and Go harness directly: genuine Replay-present-before/absent-after plus CSV and console-error assertions, not a weaker proxy. Read docs/EVENT_DETAILS_PURGE.md and confirmed every binding security statement from goal.md section 7 is present. Independently re-verified the Builder's commit signature via git log -1 --format=fuller --show-signature run through WSL (where gpg is actually available): Good signature, correct author/committer, zero Copilot mentions. No issues found.
